newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index closes at record high.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index closes at record high.

text.p: Late-session buying in Petron Corp on Friday pulled up the Manila share index which was moving sideways for most of the session, to close at a record high of 3,421.91 points, traders said.

"Normally in a bull run, we see the index flat or even slightly down with activity picking up towards close, and that was what happened today," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity.

The main index ended at 3,421.91 points, up 29.15, or 0.86 percent. This is the third time within the week that the index has surged to record highs. One was an intra-day high while on two days the index posted record closing levels.

"We closed very strong and with value turnover exceeding three billion pesos the past three days, foreign buying has swamped our market, enhancing our liquidity," said Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities.
Value turnover was heavy at 4.617 billion pesos on Friday with gainers beating losers 78 to 61 and 65 issues unchanged.
Petron closed up 50 centavos at 12 pesos with 22.49 million shares traded. Traders said secondliner Megaworld also gained substantially in late session.
Lozada said the market may see some consolidation next week with local Chinese investors cashing in gains before the Chinese New Year on February 7.
Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities, said after a brief respite, the market will continue its uptrend and aim for a 3,600 point index in the first quarter.
